 Follow us on Facebook Twitter Hello Latest news Several states are preparing to raise their minimum wages early next year. Here is the complete list, along with the new hourly rates.
 Getty Images Money From California to Michigan: states in the United States that are increasing their minimum wage as of Jan. 1, 2027
 Corina González twitter Greg Heilman Update: Nov 13th, 2026 07:47 EST 0 Share facebook twitter whatsapp Make us preferred on Google Although the federal minimum wage in the United States remains at $7.25 per hour, individual states can set their own rates. Next year, several states with minimum wages above the federal level will implement increases.
 Some states with higher-than-federal minimum wages have already raised their rates at least once. Others have automatic increases built into their laws, while some tie annual adjustments to inflation to help protect workers’ purchasing power.
 Which states will raise their minimum wage in 2027? 
 Several states will increase their minimum wage starting January 1, 2027, while others will implement increases later in the year. Some cities and counties across the country will also raise their minimum wages in January or July.
 The following states will increase their minimum wage on January 1, 2027 , with the new hourly rates listed below:
 Arizona: Will increase to $15.65 starting January 1, 2027. 
 California : $17.40 starting January 1, 2027. 
 Colorado: $15.71 starting January 1, 2027. 
 Connecticut: $17.48 starting January 1, 2027. 
 South Dakota: $12.30 starting January 1, 2027. 
 Maine: $15.70 starting January 1, 2027. 
 Michigan: $15.00 starting January 1, 2027. 
 Minnesota: $11.87 starting January 1, 2027. 
 Montana: $11.20 starting January 1, 2027. 
 Nebraska: $15.26 starting January 1, 2027. 
 New Jersey: $16.48 starting January 1, 2027. 
 Ohio: $11.40 starting January 1, 2027. 
 Rhode Island: $17.00 starting January 1, 2027. 
 Vermont: Will increase to $14.91 starting January 1, 2027. 
 Virginia: $13.75 starting January 1, 2027. 
 Washington: $17.73 starting January 1, 2027. 
 These states will also increase their minimum wages in 2027: 
 Alaska: Will raise its minimum wage to $15.00 per hour on July 1, 2027. 
 Oregon: Will increase its minimum wage in July, although the new rate has not yet been confirmed. 
 New York’s Special Case 
 New York state law had called for a minimum wage increase in 2027. However, the legislation includes a provision suspending the increase if the state’s unemployment rate reaches a specific threshold. That threshold has been reached, meaning New York’s minimum wage will not increase in January 2027.
 Nevertheless, Governor Kathy Hochul has proposed implementing the increase in March. If the proposal is approved by the state Legislature, New York’s minimum wage would increase as follows starting March 1, 2027: 
 $17.60 per hour in New York City, Long Island, and Westchester County. 
 $16.55 per hour in the rest of New York State. 
 $20.30 per hour for home health care workers in New York City, Long Island, and Westchester County. 
 $19.30 per hour for home health care workers in the rest of New York State.
